# Decisions log

Decisions made autonomously while the owner was AFK. Each line: decision — reason.

## Owner-approved (2026-10-10)
- Locus theme: purple buttons use #280A38 text; dark-mode table header #533B60; code font JetBrains Mono; comment highlight keeps 2px stripe.
- Storage: `node:sqlite` + FTS5; migration is a script, tested on a copy of real data only.
- Cover images: PNG via @resvg/resvg-js. Real Slack unfurls are not tested.
- Single draft PR, one green commit per item. Security hardening out of scope.

## Defaults applied
- Named readers = self-declared reviewer name (no auth exists).
- Legacy sessions (no edit token) stay link-editable.
- GitHub Pages path routes via 404.html SPA fallback.

## Spec reconciliation (2026-10-10, see specs/00-cross-cutting.md and BUILD-ORDER.md)
- View toggle = one `view-toggle` group with `view-toggle-read|edit|split`, labels Read/Edit/Split — replaces Edit/Preview; existing `has-text("Edit")` selectors keep working, `"Preview"` ones move to `view-toggle-read`.
- `AppToast`/`AppMenu`/`useDocState`/`DocView` are built by #2 (first consumer), not #10/#1 — needed by the foundation wave.
- `EditorToolbar` owned by #8; `focus-mode-btn` lives in it (not the header) so it survives focus mode.
- Pasted table = 2 undo steps (raw paste, then pre-paste); slash insert = 1 step back to `/query`.
- One search endpoint: `GET /library/docs` (list + FTS, segment snippets); `GET /search` dropped; #20 implements it.
- `docTitle` precedence: sessionName > front-matter title / HTML `<title>` > first human-visible H1 > filename > Untitled (FE and server).
- Handed-out server URLs use `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` only when explicitly set, else `FRONTEND_URL`; FE-built links always use the page origin.
- Reader identity: `reader_id` (anon-uuid) for reactions/views; `reader_key` = `name:<lower name>` else reader_id for pins, header percent-encoded.
- Front-matter absolute line numbers fixed by #5 (first useMarkdown item), not #7.
- All UI view changes use `replaceState` (incl. slides entry); Back never steps through views.
- `?` shortcuts overlay only in edit/split views; Esc layering and z-index scale centralised in 00 §3.
- Viewers have no `share-btn`/share dialog; they use `copy-link-btn`.
- #20 (orchestrator): live data contains one corrupt stray file `oldformat12345.json` (a test artifact, not valid JSON). The migration keeps strict behaviour (reports it, exits non-zero); the PR's deploy steps tell the operator to delete that file first. The live data dir is never modified by the build.
- #2/#4 (orchestrator ruling): a pinned revision `/d/<id>@<hash>` never GETs the live `/paste/<id>` (AC-04.15 checks the pathname). It gets content from `/paste/<id>/revisions/<hash>`, comments from `/paste/<id>/comments`, approval from the approval endpoint, and the doc `mode` from a new additive `mode` field on the revision response (owned by #2).
- #2 (orchestrator ruling): menus focus the checked item if there is one, else the first (00 §3.2 wins over AC-02.17's wording).
- #2 (orchestrator ruling): #2 adds `data-testid="theme-toggle"` to the existing theme button; #1 then rebuilds the control around it.
- #2: durable-sync e2e expectations of a visible "✓ Saved" change to "save finished, save-state hidden" (spec rule 5); this is a listed pre-existing test change.

## Implementation decisions
- #4: UI view toggles do not write `?view=` yet — they *drop* a present `view` param (replaceState) so a reload/copied link cannot reopen a stale view; unknown/forbidden/empty values are rewritten to `view=read` and `?view=edit` is honoured on load. Writing the toggle into the URL reopens edit view after a reload, which breaks durable-sync.test.mjs:165-169 and :212-215 (they reload in edit view and expect `.preview-pane`) — #2/#7 (ViewToggle owners) wire it with that test change.
- #4: frame→parent `anchor-changed` with `id: ''` clears the fragment (rule 15's in-frame `href="#"`); otherwise only ids of 1–256 chars are accepted. Frame-driven fragment updates are coalesced to ≤ 2/s and dropped if the route changed meanwhile; every history call is try/caught (Safari throws past its rate limit).
- #4: one leave rule (rule 13): any navigation away from the attached shared doc with unsaved changes (link, Back/Forward, library, New, not-found) flushes autosave for ≤ 1.5 s while the doc stays on screen, then `confirm()`s. Cancel pushes the doc URL back; accepting discards the edits (detach + drop the persisted draft), so later navigation does not ask again.
- #4: drafts: the main draft slot only ever holds what the current route shows (paused otherwise), and the never-shared local draft also lives in its own slot (`md-review-local-draft`), so opening a shared doc never costs it. The landing route shows that local draft when arriving from elsewhere; sharing a local doc (or New on it) forgets it; New from a shared doc keeps it in storage. An all-empty screen writes nothing. Exception kept from before: a doc that answers 404/410 while this browser holds its draft turns that copy into the local doc.
- #4: slugs are matched case-sensitively by the server (`/d/Weekly` ≠ `/d/weekly` → doc-not-found); left as-is.
- #4: local-draft persistence is paused on pinned-revision, file and embed views so viewing them never overwrites the reader's own draft.
- #4: pinned and file routes use a read-only header (no Edit/Preview, Save, History, Share, Generate Prompt, New, rename); the pinned header shows the doc id as its name (the revision API has no filename).
- #4: a doc that answers 404/410 while this browser holds its draft keeps the "Showing your local copy" notice and moves to the landing route (replaceState), where a local doc lives.
- Build order (orchestrator): #20 lands before #2 instead of after it. #20 changes no frontend code and its golden tests treat `mode` as an allowed additive field. #2 was built against the JSON server and then ported onto #20's route modules: one helper, `server/mode.cjs` (validation, default, `modeOf` for legacy rows), used by paste-create, session (PUT meta + GETs), list, revisions and library-docs, on top of the pure `shared/docMode.mjs` that the FE uses too.
- #5 (test author): `src/composables/useDocTitle.ts` exports `docTitle({sessionName, content, contentType, filename})` (00 §5 order, whitespace collapsed, no truncation), `truncateTitle(title, max=80)` (cut + `…`), `formatDocumentTitle(title)` → `<title> · md-review`.
- #8 (test author): `src/composables/useExternalChange.ts` exports `minimalChange(oldText, newText)` → `null` when equal, else one `{from, to, insert}` covering only the changed span.
- #3 (test author): `src/markdown/headingIds.ts` exports `slugify(text)`, `assignIds(texts[])`, `extractHeadings(source)` → `{level,id,text}[]` (same ids as rendered), `buildToc(headings)` → `{id,text,level,depth}[]` (drops a lone leading H1, levels 1–3, `[]` when < 2). Slugs match github-slugger@2.0.0.
- #9 (test author): `src/editor/markdownCommands.ts` exports CodeMirror state commands `toggleBold`, `toggleItalic`, `toggleStrikethrough`, `toggleCode`, `toggleLink`.
- Scope add (orchestrator): QA on #4 found two PRE-EXISTING sync bugs (also on master 65d5a29). (1) Major: after a 412 conflict, a reload/close+reopen forgets the conflict state ("Unsaved changes"), and the next save PUTs with the collaborator's hash as If-Match and overwrites their change. (2) Minor: with saves failing, typing then reloading within ~300 ms loses the text (draft not flushed on pagehide). Both are assigned to #8, which owns useSync's remote-change handling; the conflict state must persist with the draft and survive reload.
- Scope add: at 390 px the doc header overflows and the view toggle is unreachable — covered by #2 (header) / #5 (phone header).

## Implementation decisions
- #20: a server that refuses to boot on an un-migrated data dir must not leave an (empty) DB file behind — otherwise the next boot would pass the check and silently 404 every link (AC-20.7 test asserts it).
- #20: golden compatibility (AC-20.3) is checked against responses frozen from the JSON-file server at 592efa6 (`server/test-items/fixtures/20/goldens.json`); allowed differences are ETag values, run-generated ids/timestamps, file-list order (legacy order is readdir order), 400 instead of the legacy 500 for an invalid `/paste/list?name=` regex, `content_hash`/`comments: []` added where legacy omitted them, the additive keys of rule 5 / 00 §10.5, and `mode` per 00 §1.4 — because these are the only differences the spec allows or that are filesystem noise.
- #20: a slug present in both `_slug-index.json` (session) and `_site-index.json` (site) keeps the legacy split: `slugs` row points at the session, the site still resolves by its own `sites.slug` — matches the JSON server's `resolveId` / `resolveSiteId`.
- #20: a site directory with no `_site-index.json` entry (the live data has one) is still served at `/site/<id>/` and stays out of `/site/list`, as the JSON server does.
- #20: a corrupt revision blob in the DB answers 500 `…unreadable…`, never empty content — the DB-era form of `server/test.mjs:550-562`.
- #20: `match.field` names where the snippet came from. A title (else filename) hit is shown unless the body excerpt has hit words the title does not show, case aside ("café" for a "Cafe notes" title — R-20.6 expects that body hit); then the body excerpt is shown with `field: content`. Snippets are plain text (markdown syntax stripped, whitespace collapsed, HTML entities decoded) and the body scan is capped at 256 KB per result.
- #20: snippets are cut in JS with a unicode61-like folding tokenizer instead of FTS5 `snippet()`/`highlight()` — those are quadratic in the number of hits (a 5 MB doc with 220k hits took 142 s; now 14 ms).
- #20: `/library/docs` answers 400 `{error:'invalid mode'|'invalid type'|'invalid updated_after'}` for malformed values (00 §8 only names sort/cursor); unknown collection/tag → `items: []` as specified. The cursor is an opaque offset bound to q + filters + effective sort; a different `limit` with a cursor is allowed.
- #20: library `updated_at` (sort + `updated_after`) is what `/paste/list` always reported: latest revision `at_end || at`, else `sharedAt`; comment/approval/meta writes do not bump it.
- #20: `POST /paste` stores `mode` (00 §1.4 default; an invalid value fell back to the default; since #2 it is a 400) and the creator's `author` as `created_by`; `GET /paste/:id` returns `mode` (additive) but not `created_by` (#26 exposes it).
- #20: legacy sessions that never stored a `content_hash` keep omitting it and are not seeded from '' on their first write (`contents.hashless`) — what the JSON server did.
- #20: every slug delete is scoped to its owner (`AND target_id = ?`): deleting a site or session, or releasing a slug via `PUT /meta`, never frees another doc's slug (the JSON server dropped index entries by name).
- #20: the migration skips a session whose revision blob is missing, unreadable or does not match its hash (reported under `errors`, exit ≠ 0) rather than importing it without that revision.
- #20: `GET /paste/list?name=<invalid regex>` → 400 `{error:'Invalid name pattern'}` (legacy 500); `GET /paste/:id` ETag = md5(id, write version, content hash), so it changes on every write including file writes.
- #20: client-supplied meta keys named like server-managed columns (`edit_token_hash`, `upsert_key`, `created_by`, `from_template_json`, `version`, `title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `id`, …) are dropped on write and by the migration, never kept in `extra_json` — a forged `edit_token_hash` must not round-trip.
- #20: the migration is a pre-cutover tool: each session is written and verified in one transaction (rolled back on failure); `schema_meta.migration_complete` is set only after a run whose only errors are reported corrupt sources, and the server refuses to boot on a DB whose migration started but did not complete (even with `ALLOW_EMPTY_DB=1`). A session the server wrote after migration (`version > 1`) is reported `diverged` and left alone; a session deleted after cutover would be re-imported by a re-run, so the script is not run after cutover.
- #20 (perf): the indexed text, snippet text and docTitle are computed in linear time — tags, comments, raw-text elements and markdown links are found with forward-only indexOf scans, `_emphasis_` and ATX headings are parsed by hand, and the table-delimiter and list-bullet rules no longer rescan across lines (the regex versions took 6–122 s on 600 KB docs such as `'<script'×90k` or `'[a'×300k`). Output is unchanged on the #20 fixtures, the repo docs, the live data dir and 100k fuzzed inputs compared against the regex versions.
- #22: the bundled fonts are static Regular/SemiBold instances cut (fontTools instancer) from google/fonts `ofl/montserrat/Montserrat[wght].ttf` — google/fonts ships only the variable file and resvg ignores variable axes (every weight rendered as Thin); OFL.txt is bundled beside them. System fonts are never loaded.
- #22: the cover draws only what the bundled font can: emoji (incl. ZWJ sequences, modifiers, flags, variation selectors, keycaps) and characters Montserrat has no glyph for are removed from the cover title and author; when no letter or digit is left the cover shows the filename (without extension), else "Markdown document"/"HTML document". cover_key is computed from the drawn title and meta line, so two docs whose covers look the same share a key. Page text (og:title etc.) is unaffected.
- #22: the meta page ETag also covers `article:modified_time`, the redirect target (query) and the canonical URL, not only (title, description, cover_key, variant) — otherwise a body edit or another query string could answer 304 with a stale page. `If-None-Match: *` answers 304 for an existing doc (page and cover).
- #22: the cover's "Updated" date is the UTC day of `updated_at`; "by" is the first non-seeded revision's author, else `created_by` — never a client label (api/mcp/ui); it is left out when unknown and cut with "…" when it would push the date off the cover.
- #22: `/d/:x/:file` pages describe the file itself (its own docTitle/description for .md/.markdown/.txt/.html files; a "file from …" line otherwise) and reuse the doc's cover. Pinned `/d/:x@:rev` pages describe that revision (its title, description and revision time) and carry no og:image (`twitter:card summary`) — the only cover is the live doc's, which could contradict the revision. An unknown revision or unlisted file is the doc's 404 page; an unparseable `/d/` path (dot or empty segments, encoded slashes, `@rev` plus a file, a malformed rev) is a 404 page that sends humans to the app root `FRONTEND_URL/d/`, never echoing the raw path.
- #22: meta-page and cover text look at the first 256 KB of a doc (`SCAN_CAP`); HTML is scanned with indexOf (no lazy cross-tag regexes), line/paragraph regexes see at most 1 KB, and rule 4c looks for the first visible paragraph among the first 500 blocks — so extraction is linear (a 1 MB pathological doc < 50 ms). The H1 title now decodes entities and honours backslash escapes (also in the #20 search title); a leading BOM is ignored; a doc without `contentType` named `*.html`/`*.htm` is treated as HTML for the meta page and cover.
- #22: one link rule: `POST /paste` and `GET /paste/:id` (full, or `?fields=` with meta) return `url` = `handedOutUrl(slug || id)` (`server/links.cjs`); MCP `shareUrl` and CLI `url` use the backend's `url` and fall back to `docUrl(PUBLIC_BASE_URL || FRONTEND_URL, x)` from their own env for an older backend. An explicit CLI `--frontend` wins over both. The HTTP MCP server reads PUBLIC_BASE_URL too.
- #2: save-state renders in the editor header only (00 §2.2 wins over #2 rule 5's "all columns" row); the read view shows conflicts through `conflict-bar` as before. durable-sync's restore test now watches the server instead of a read-view save-state.
- #2: on a pinned revision of a review doc (viewer) the sidebar lists the doc's comments (`GET /paste/:id/comments`) and the approval banner shows the doc's status with "Open the latest version to approve or request changes" instead of actions (an approval from an old revision was misleading, and local-only resolves could enable a button the server then refused). Selecting text does not start a new comment — its line numbers would anchor to an old revision — and sidebar edits stay local (no live session before #23).
- #2: History on a pinned revision compares against that revision ("now" = what is on screen); the default "from" is the revision before it. Restore stays editor-only.
- #2: file routes (`/d/:x/:file`) keep #4's viewer capability and open in publish mode (a session file has no comments of its own); revisit with #26/#23.
- #2: the History revision count and unseen-changes dot moved onto the `menu-history` item (badge + `.history-dot`); `history-button` is retired.
- #2: `AppMode` is now `'upload' | 'doc' | 'dashboard'`; usePersistence's callback keeps its old `'review'` value (mapped to `'doc'` in useDocState) so its unit tests stay untouched.
- #2: a mode PUT in flight, or one that settled after a poll's request started, wins over that poll's `mode` (no flicker back on a fast toggle); the server value is authoritative from the next poll on.
- #2: phone (<641px) demotes app-home-link, nav-library, reviewer-name, share-btn and copy-link-btn to the overflow menu and makes the view toggle icon-only; tablet demotes reviewer-name; reader meta moves to `doc-meta-row` below 1100px. #5 owns the rest of the phone layout.
- #2: the pinned-revision header title is the doc's sessionName || filename: `GET /paste/:id/revisions/:hash` additively returns `sessionName` and `filename` next to `mode` (same reason as the mode ruling: a pinned revision never GETs /paste/<id>).
- #2: the below-header stack renders in 00 §2.4 order (pinned → conflict/persist-error → notice → approval/summary → changes); before #2 approval/summary/changes came above the notice and conflict bars.
- #2: mode writes are serialised (one PUT in flight; the latest choice is written next; a failure rolls back with a toast only if nothing newer is pending, so no error toast when the final state succeeded).
- #2: FE + server share `shared/docMode.mjs` (00 §4.8) through a new `@shared` alias (vite + tsconfig paths; a `.d.mts` gives the FE its types); the server loads it with `require()` (Node ≥ 22 `require(esm)`).
- #2: toasts keep their status/alert role but set `aria-live="off"`; two always-present sr-only live regions (polite, assertive) announce the newest toast text, and hovering or focusing a toast pauses its auto-dismiss.
- #2: the leave-page handlers (beforeunload/pagehide/visibilitychange autosave flush) moved from App.vue into useAutosave; the comment-file import errors use toasts instead of alert().
- #6: the editor slot is a thin `LazyEditor.vue` wrapper (placeholder / error / retry, attrs passed through to EditorPane) over one shared loader (`useEditorLoader.ts`), not a bare `defineAsyncComponent` — retry and the stale-deploy diagnosis need state `defineAsyncComponent` doesn't expose, and EditorPane stays untouched apart from an exposed `focus()`.
- #6: retry re-imports the EditorPane URL named in the failed import's error with a `?retry=N` cache-bust (browsers keep failed module fetches) and takes the component from `default` (or the export whose `__name` is EditorPane); after a failure, hover/focus prefetch stays quiet until an explicit Edit/Retry. "Stale deployment" = a `HEAD` on that URL returns 404/410; when the error names no URL (Safari), a no-store fetch of index.html whose entry script differs from the running one. A network error = offline, no reload hint. Focus moves into the editor only on its first mount, not on later warm read → edit switches (same as before #6, where a fresh editor never took focus).
- #6: `vite.config.ts` puts every node_modules module EditorPane statically needs (and the entry doesn't) into a `codemirror` vendor chunk (`manualChunks`, computed from the module graph; Vite's preload helper pinned to its own tiny chunk so the entry never imports the vendor chunk). The EditorPane chunk is then a 4 kB facade with a `default` export and the language-data chunks import CodeMirror from the vendor chunk, so a cache-busted retry never creates a second CodeMirror.
- #6: the kept-alive editor is keyed on the doc on screen (`screenKey|pasteId`): another document drops the instance (and any per-doc editor state such as #8 history); a local doc replaced through the file picker keeps the `landing` key and therefore the instance (its v-model content is replaced).
- #23: a `?edit=` token is held in memory until the doc's GET (sent with it) answers `access.can_edit: true`, and only then stored, under the `id` the GET returned — a token for another doc is never stored; a stored token a GET no longer accepts is dropped — rule 9 + the "token for a different doc" edge case.
- #23: GET /paste/:id's ETag varies with the caller's access on protected docs (view vs edit), and rotation/claim bumps the session version — otherwise a poller's 304 would keep a stale `access` after a rotation.
- #23: chunk/complete only accept an upload started on the same doc (else 404 "Upload not found"), and uploadIds must be hex — otherwise chunks could be pushed into a protected doc's upload through a legacy doc's URL, bypassing the guard.
- #23: the expiry picker preselects the value last applied in this dialog, else "Never" for a doc without expiry, else the smallest option covering the time left — the server stores only `expires_at`, not the chosen day count; the label always shows the real date.
- #23: opening History on a live doc refreshes the revision list, and Escape closes the History and Share dialogs — AC-23.9 waits for the list request and closes History with Escape.
- #23: pre-#23 test suites keep their intent through one mechanism each: e2e suites create link-editable (legacy) docs via `tests/e2e/lib/legacy-docs.mjs`; server suites opt in to `server/test-items/lib/edit-token-jar.mjs`, which presents each doc's own token on writes. #23's own tests use neither.
- #23: verify.sh exports `MCP_TOKEN_STORE` under the run dir so no test writes the repo default `server/mcp-state/`.
- #23 (review round): losing edit access — a write refused with 401/403 or a poll answering `can_edit: false` — runs one handler: view-only toast (once), viewer, read view, `?view=edit|split` rewritten to `view=read`.
- #23 (review round): edits that never reached the server when a doc turns view-only become an unsaved *local copy* (`md-review-local-copies` localStorage map, {[docId]: {markdown, filename, at}}), shown in a banner below the header ("Your unsaved changes (not on the server)", testids `local-copy-banner|toggle|copy|download|discard|body`) while the doc shows the server version; a reload as viewer turns an unsaved draft into that copy too. The copy renders inside `.preview-pane` (the shared preview styles), expanded by default.
- #23 (review round): for a viewer, autosave, keepalive writes on pagehide, the leave-page prompt and the discard confirmation are skipped; a 401/403 save is not a save error.
- #23 (review round): useEditToken's router hook is registered explicitly by App.vue (`installEditTokenHook()` before `router.bootstrap()`), not as an import side effect.
- #23 (review round): e2e `createDoc({ protected: true })` returns `editToken` (open with `?edit=`); the legacy default stays for unrelated suites. The #6 lazy-chunk part of the viewer ACs waits for #6; 23-fixes checks that a protected viewer never gets an editor.
- #23: MCP token-store keys are `${pasteApiUrl}|${idOrSlug}` (trailing slash trimmed); bare pre-scoping keys are read as a fallback and replaced by the scoped key on the next save of that doc — two backends' docs with the same id or slug must not share a token.
- #23: token-store writes take an O_EXCL lock file (`${file}.lock`; stale after 5 s; after 3 s of waiting the writer goes ahead) and re-read + merge before the atomic rename — concurrent stdio/HTTP MCP processes must not drop each other's entries.
- #23: MCP shell commands use `PASTE_PUBLIC_URL`, else `PASTE_API_URL` (both transports); the hard-coded `10.0.99.151:3100` default is removed; trailing slashes in the configured URLs are ignored.
- #23: GET /paste/:id sends `Vary: Authorization, X-Edit-Token` (200 and 304); create and rotate/claim responses are `Cache-Control: no-store` (they carry the raw token). The #20 golden comparison accepts that header on token-carrying responses.
- #23 (integration): a viewer never keeps #6's hidden editor — `editorShown` requires capability editor and losing edit access unmounts the kept editor slot.
- #8: write origin is explicit — writers call `markExternalChange(text, 'remote'|'local')` (useExternalChange.ts) right before assigning `markdown`; an unmarked external write is treated as remote (minimal change, out of history, history cleared). Only revision restore is marked `local` (one line in DocView.vue's restore handler).
- #8: until #6/#7 keep the editor mounted, history survives a Read↔Edit switch by keeping the editor's selection + history (`state.toJSON({history})`) on unmount and restoring it on the next mount, only for the same text and when no barrier (remote write, pasteId change) happened meanwhile. Works unchanged if #6 keeps the instance alive.
- #8: the SVG paste handler moved from EditorPane into `src/editor/svgPaste.ts` (listed in extensions.ts) so later paste modules slot in by order; it is tagged `input.paste`, and every paste/drop is history-isolated by a transactionExtender.
- #8 (scope add 1): a conflicted draft persists `serverMarkdown` = the copy the edits were based on, its `baseHash`, and `conflict: true`; on load `restoreDraft` keeps that base as the If-Match baseline and the fresh server copy as the remote side (before, the fresh copy became the baseline, so the next reload showed "Unsaved changes" and the next save overwrote the collaborator).
- #8 (scope add 2): on pagehide / beforeunload / visibilitychange→hidden the draft snapshot is also written synchronously to localStorage (existing keys `md-review-state` / `md-review-local-draft`); the next load takes whichever of that and the IndexedDB copy has the newer `savedAt`, then removes the localStorage copy. Snapshots too big for localStorage still get the async IndexedDB attempt.
- #8 (fix round): document undo/redo runs only while the editor has focus or from the toolbar. Chrome forwards a native undo/redo pressed in another text field (filename, reviewer name) with nothing left to undo there to the last edited contenteditable as a `historyUndo`/`historyRedo` beforeinput; a highest-precedence handler swallows those when the editor is not focused. App's only global key handler is Mod+S.
- #8 (fix round): remote writes are applied as one change per changed region (`minimalChanges`: line diff of the span between common prefix/suffix via `diff`, each hunk trimmed to its differing characters, all in one transaction), so a caret or scroll anchor between distant edits maps through untouched. More than 2000 changed lines falls back to the single span. `minimalChange` (single span, frozen contract) is unchanged.
- #8 (fix round): a revision restore done from Read view is not undoable until #6 keeps the editor mounted — the restored text differs from the kept editor state, so the next Edit view starts with a fresh history.
- #8 (fix round): multi-cursor is not enabled (CodeMirror's `allowMultipleSelections` stays off), so the "multi-cursor edit undone in one step" edge case does not apply; enabling it is a separate product call.
- #8 (fix round): every local document switch (file load, New/reset, landing local draft) calls `historyBarrier()`, so history kept across a view switch never comes back for a different doc with identical text. The localStorage flush copy is removed once the async write of that same snapshot lands; the beforeunload flush listener was dropped (pagehide covers reload, close and bfcache). Since #2 there is one leave-page path: useAutosave's pagehide / visibilitychange→hidden handler first calls `usePersistence.flushDraft()` (synchronous local-draft copy), then sends dirty shared edits with keepalive; usePersistence registers no window listeners of its own.
- #9: Tab/Shift+Tab renumber the ordered lists they touch in the same undo step: a nested ordered list counts from 1 (CommonMark lets only `1.` interrupt the parent item's paragraph, so `   2. b` under `1. a` would render as text), a top-level one keeps its first number and stays consecutive; siblings left behind by an outdent restart at 1 under the moved item. Nested lists that started at another number are reset to 1 when touched.
- #9: multi-cursor stays off in the editor (#8 decision); the commands act on every range (unit-tested with `allowMultipleSelections`), so turning it on later needs no change here.
- #9: the overlay's focus trap is inline in `ShortcutsOverlay.vue` until #3's `useFocusTrap` exists. `?` opens it only while an `EditorToolbar` is on screen (registered host element with client rects) — the editor may stay mounted but hidden (#6 keep-alive), so mounted is not enough; the `?` entry (`shortcutsHelpShortcut`) is one line in App.vue's `useGlobalShortcuts` list and does its own gating/preventDefault so a `?` typed into an input is never swallowed.
- #9: the shortcuts button's overlay returns focus to the button on close (AC-09.16), the one exception to "toolbar buttons refocus the editor" (00 §3.3).
- #9 (fix round): block markup (`> `, `#…# `, `- `/`* `/`+ `, `N.`/`N)`, task box) stays outside emphasis/link/code markers, single- and multi-line. A selection that already contains the marker (`**a** and **b**`) is made one span — inner markers removed, whole wrapped — like Docs bolding a partly bold selection; a multi-line toggle decides wrap/unwrap once, from the first non-empty line. Mod+E unfences only when both fences belong to one FencedCode node. Mod+K escapes `[`/`]` in the label (and unescapes on unwrap).
- #9 (fix round): EditorPane's deferred selection report clamps its position to the current doc and skips a destroyed view (pre-existing "No tile at position N" page error when the doc shrank before the next frame); toolbar Undo/Redo titles now come from shortcutList's `formatCombo`, same labels and order as the overlay.
- #8 (landing on #6): `historyBarrier()` also clears a mounted editor's live history (`onHistoryBarrier` → `clearHistory`), because #6 keeps one editor instance across a local file replacement on the landing key and identical text never reaches the content watcher. #8's keep/restore-across-unmount stays (still used when #6's keyed instance is dropped and re-created for the same doc, gated by text + epoch); it is redundant for plain Read↔Edit switches now and could be removed later. (Code amended into the #8 commit; this line is uncommitted with #9.)
- #1: new theme tokens `--accent-text` / `--text-meta` (= `--accent` / `--text-muted` everywhere except Locus: #533B60 in locus-light, #B066FF / #9B8FA8 in locus-dark) carry accent-as-text and small meta text (logo `.oss`, Review badge, reviewer name, doc-updated, summary/sidebar/banner/library meta), so brand tokens keep their spec values while chrome text passes AA.
- #1: comment categories are tokens `--cat-<name>` (hue, used as text and as a fill) + `--cat-<name>-on` (text on that fill), set per theme at >= 4.5:1; dark themes use light hues with dark text (the old must-fix-only dark override is folded in). Locus: suggestion #3264FF, question #280A38 (light) / #B066FF (dark), nit = `--text-meta`; must-fix stays a status red. `CategoryMeta` gains `onColor`.
- #1: an inline `<head>` script in index.html applies the stored theme (classes + data-theme-style) before first paint; tests/composables/themeBoot.test.ts runs it against applyTheme() for every value so the two cannot drift.
- #1: the library and not-found pages get a slim `app-bar` with the theme switcher (they have no doc header).
- #1: Montserrat 300 stays in the font request: the frozen rule-8 test asserts the exact `0,300;0,400;0,500;0,600;0,800;1,400` axes.
- #1: AppMenu draws the radio dot with CSS (`::before`) so a menuitemradio's text is exactly its label, takes optional per-entry `attrs` (used for `data-style`) and a `menuLabel` for a list name that differs from the trigger's; the header lets any open `role=menu` escape its box, not only the overflow menu.
- #1: the Style menu (3 items) does not clip its overflow and carries a square transparent hit area, so its rounded corners count as inside the menu (an outside click on a corner pixel does not close it).
- #1: mermaid renders are serialised and coalesced, and each diagram is drawn off-DOM with `mermaid.render` and swapped in with one `innerHTML` assignment, skipped when its source + theme config are unchanged (`data-rendered-key`). No re-render ever empties a diagram (a half-built or empty SVG was visible to readers and tests mid-render). A diagram that fails to parse shows a plain "Diagram error: …" line instead of mermaid's error graphic.
- #1 (pre-existing #2 race, surfaced by the gate under load): RevisionsModal is a lazy chunk; opened before the chunk loaded, it mounted already visible and its non-immediate `visible` watcher never loaded the diff (durable-sync "changes since you last looked"). The watcher is now `immediate`, and only the latest of overlapping loads writes its result.
- #1: the #1a extraction keeps the base `.preview-pane` rule at its old scoped specificity via `:root .preview-pane`, otherwise github-markdown-css's `.markdown-body` (same specificity, later in the cascade) would win in GitHub mode; 8 before/after full-page screenshots were byte-identical.
- #1: Locus xy charts take the page background with brand axis/label colours (mermaid's xyChart defaults to a white canvas and black axes).
- #1 (gate infra): vite's pre-bundled dep cache moves per worktree (`VITE_CACHE_DIR` = `.verify/vite-cache`, set by scripts/lib/stack.sh): all worktrees share one node_modules (symlink), so concurrent dev servers rewrote the same `node_modules/.vite/deps` and lazy mermaid diagram chunks 404'd mid-run ("Failed to fetch dynamically imported module …/pieDiagram-….js?v=…"); that was the cause of the AC-01.9 "0 legend swatches" failure in the main worktree.
- #5: `src/composables/useFocusTrap.ts` (00 §3.4 names #3 as its builder) lands with #5, because #5's comments drawer is the first drawer and claims `aria-modal`; it only cycles Tab/Shift+Tab inside the container and moves/returns focus (it does not pull back focus that leaves by other means — that would fight useShortcutsOverlay returning focus before unmount). #3 reuses it for the TOC drawer and #9's overlay.
- #5: print tables are `width: 100%` with cells `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (paper has no sideways scroll box); on screen cells keep `break-word` (below).
- #5: table cells use `overflow-wrap: break-word`, not `anywhere` (rule 5 lists cells with `anywhere`) — `anywhere` lowers a cell's min-content width to one character, so a wide table would squeeze every column instead of scrolling inside its `table-scroll` (AC-05.2 needs it to scroll).
- #5: document scroll (rule 2) applies to the read view of markdown docs; HTML (iframe) docs and file views keep the fixed layout so the iframe "fills the remaining height" (rule 5) — the iframe has its own scroll.
- #5: front-matter body lines stay absolute by rendering the body with the front-matter lines blanked out (same line count), not by re-mapping token ranges; `getLineMap` does the same.
- #5: print rules live in `src/styles/print.css`, imported last from `main.ts` (after `style.css`), so #19 can reuse/inline one file; colours use `!important` because the GitHub sheets are runtime `<link>`s that load after it.
- #5: the light mermaid copy for print is rendered in idle time after a dark render and swapped in synchronously on `beforeprint` (a real Ctrl+P snapshots right after the event); afterprint restores the screen SVG and its bound handlers.
- #5: `comments-toggle` counts all comments (resolved included, as the sidebar title does); tapping a comment in the drawer closes the sheet so its line is visible. Below 1100px the sidebar's collapse state is ignored.
- #5: docTitle re-parses the markdown 300 ms after the last keystroke in the editor (immediately for loads/polls), keeping the 1 s rule without a parse per key. Truncation counts code points so an emoji is never split.
- #5: on phone the editor header's save state is a status dot (label kept for AT) and Save is an icon button (00 §2.2 "✓ (icon)").
- #3: slugs use the Unicode-property form of github-slugger's rule (`[^\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}\p{Pc}\- ]` removed) instead of adding the dependency; the frozen table (incl. Greek/Cyrillic/Korean/Arabic, skin-tone emoji) matches github-slugger@2.0.0.
- #3: the headingIds plugin also records the heading list in markdown-it's `env`, so PreviewPane gets ids + plain text from the same parse as the HTML (`renderWithHeadings`); `extractHeadings` (TOC, docTitle) parses with the preview's own markdown-it instance, so later plugins (#16/#28/#12) can never make TOC text/ids drift from the render. The TOC parses only while a TOC can show.
- #3: ids are slugged from the heading text *before* typographer replacements (`foo--bar` → `foo--bar`, `(c) note` → `c-note`, as on GitHub); TOC/label text is the rendered text (after them).
- #3: a TOC click pins its entry as active until the reader's next wheel/touch/key/mouse input or Back/Forward (rule 12 "active immediately"), so a smooth jump or the bottom rule never flips it away mid-scroll. A rebuild (poll/restore) that keeps the active id pins it the same way and scrolls by the shift so that heading stays where the reader had it (rule 14; content inserted above no longer pushes the reading position).
- #3: the drawer's "page does not scroll" is `overflow: hidden` on <html> while it is open (restored on close/unmount/resize to desktop).
- #3: copying a section link does `setFragment(id, 'replace', 'frame')` — the 'frame' source tells PreviewPane's route watcher the reader is already there (no scroll), as for iframe anchor updates.
- #3: in the document-scroll layout `scrollToAnchorElement` uses `scrollIntoView({block:'start'})` and every `.preview-pane [id]` has `scroll-margin-top: header + 12px`, so JS jumps and native fragment navigation land at the same offset (was: scrollTo(top − header height), which also matched a raw `<header>` in doc content and could round a sub-pixel under the header).
- #3: the TOC drawer and #9's shortcuts overlay use #5's useFocusTrap (the overlay's inline trap is gone).
- #3: in-doc jumps after load (TOC click, link) re-align once when diagrams/images above are still pending (the #4 rule-14 realign, previously initial-load only); Back/Forward and same-document fragment navigation align on the next frame, after the browser's own fragment scroll (which picks the first element with that id in the page — `#app` for a heading named "app"). The initial realign also waits for the load event for the same reason.
- #3: app-owned element ids that a heading slug could collide with are prefixed (`md-review-toc-drawer`, `md-review-comments-drawer`; the rail has no id); `toc-toggle` carries `aria-controls` only in drawer mode (the collapsed rail is not in the DOM). `#app` stays (tests and index.html depend on it); container-scoped lookups (#4) plus the deferred align cover it.
- #3: useFocusTrap keeps a stack (only the innermost trap handles Tab), and an owner unmounting while active returns focus like a close (`returnFocus: () => false` opts out — the shortcuts overlay, whose store returns focus). Tapping a comment in the comments sheet closes it and returns focus to `comments-toggle` (standard dialog close).
- #3: EnhancerContext passes generic services (headings, docState, router, toast, copyText) plus `copySectionLink`, so #14/#15/#17/#24 add an enhancer without touching PreviewPane's call.
- #10: placeholders and images are recorded as one undo step by swapping, not by editing history: the placeholder insert is the paste's undo step; when every upload of the paste has settled, the placeholders are swapped back to what the paste replaced (outside the history) and that is swapped for the images (one isolated history step). CodeMirror maps a history event through out-of-history changes in a way that keeps the replacement text, so a direct out-of-history replacement would leave the image behind on undo (rule 10).
- #10: a multi-image paste shows its images together when the last upload settles (a failed one's placeholder goes at once). Replacing each placeholder as its own upload finishes would split the paste's undo step, so undo mid-upload could not return the pre-paste text.
- #10: a selection replaced by an image paste is taken out outside the history and put back by the paste's undo (and when every upload fails), so one undo returns the exact pre-paste text.
- #10: undo while uploads run suspends the paste (its placeholders are gone, results wait); redo brings the placeholders back — found in the redo's own inserted text, not by searching the doc — and the images land then. A placeholder deleted or edited by hand gets nothing and is left as typed.
- #10: "Share and insert" keeps the author in the editor (the share URL carries no `view`, which would otherwise switch to the read view), then inserts at the paste-time position in the editor remounted for the new doc key (waits ≤ 3 s for it, else an error toast).
- #10 (orchestrator follow-up): placeholders of uploads still running never persist — each paste registers with `attachments.ts` and every write that leaves the page (autosave, the pagehide keepalive, the local draft) sends `stripPendingPlaceholders(markdown)`: the paste found whole goes back to the text it replaced, else each placeholder goes with its joining blank line. The doc stays dirty while uploads run, so #4's leave guard / beforeunload asks before leaving. An editor that opens on a doc holding placeholders no running upload owns (an older build, another tab, a crash) removes them outside the history and autosave stores the clean doc.
- #10: a non-string `content` for an `assets/` name is a 400 `Invalid content` (not 413).
- #11: the plain-text chord stays armed through a paste event that carries no text (headless Chromium fires one for Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V before the test's paste; an image-only clipboard is not pasted either) until a paste with text, a plain Mod+V keydown (disarms it) or 1 s. The chord is matched on `event.code` too (non-Latin layouts).
- #11: the very end of a table row counts as outside the table for paste conversion — rule 1 would otherwise glue a second paste right after a pasted table (the cursor ends there, rule 8) onto its last row; the new table is isolated by a blank line (rule 8).
- #11: Shift+Alt+F inside a fenced/indented code block, or in an html doc, is "No table at cursor" (pipes in code are not a table).
- #11: the format-table command keeps the first row's indentation on every row (a table nested in a list stays nested).
- #21: an upsert-create stores only the documented body fields (markdown, filename, contentType, sessionName, slug, mode, expiry_days, author, changeNote) — other keys a POST /paste would keep in extra_json (callback_url, comments, arbitrary meta) are ignored, so a job cannot smuggle meta into a keyed doc. `mode` is validated on every upsert (uniform 400) but only applied on create.
- #21: an update whose content and filename/contentType/sessionName are unchanged reports `changed:false` even when `expiry_days` was given or an expired doc was revived; the expiry change is still saved (no new revision). Only filename/contentType/sessionName/content count as "changed".
- #21: the reserved slugs (`list`, `by-key`, 00 §6) are enforced in storage `uniqueSlug`, so POST /paste, PUT /meta and upserts all get `-2` for them.
- #21: CLI `publish` takes the token from `--token` / `MDREVIEW_EDIT_TOKEN` only (like #23's upload/patch), not the MCP token store; it prints editToken/editUrl on create. MCP `upsert_session` stores the token under `key:<key>` (+ id, slug) in the #23 store; slugs cannot contain `:`, so these entries never collide.
- #21: the MCP tools added by the view-and-share items are registered once by `registerSharedTools(server, handlers)` in mcp-server.js, called by both the stdio and the HTTP server (no duplicated schemas).
- #21 (fix round): an upsert that changes only filename/contentType/sessionName reports `changed:true` but adds no revision (revisions are content-addressed; there is nothing to diff), so its `changeNote` is not stored. `expiry_days` on an upsert follows #23 rule 8's coercion (null = never, 1/7/30/90 as given, anything else → 30), not a 400. `contentType` accepts any string, stored as POST /paste stores it.
- #21 (fix round): a later ordinary write never coalesces into a revision that carries a note (the note must keep describing its content). The response of an upsert is sent after its transaction committed. A legacy session already owning a reserved slug keeps it on PUT /meta.
- #21 (fix round): CLI `publish` sends the display filename only with `--filename` (a job writing a temp file with a random name must not flip it every run). The FE loader treats a shared doc without `filename` as '' (before, docTitle's `filename.trim()` threw and took the header — and with it History — down; pre-existing, hit by every REST/MCP upsert without a filename).
- #24: section keys are the heading ids the renderer emits today (`headingAnchorPlugin`, ASCII slugs) stored as a plain string; the server validates them with the Unicode rule (`\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}\p{Pc}` and `-`), so #3's GitHub slugger can replace the ids without a migration. Headings whose id changes under #3 simply orphan their old reactions (hidden in the UI, still in GET), as for any edited heading.
- #24: #3's preview-enhancer pipeline has not landed, so this item creates `src/preview/index.ts` (`runEnhancers`, one list) with `sectionReactions` as its first entry and one `runEnhancers` call in PreviewPane after each render; #3 adds `headingAnchors` to the same list. Section reactions sit before any `.heading-anchor`.
- #24: until #5's document-scroll layout lands, the reaction bar is the last row of the content column under the scrolling preview pane (always visible at the bottom), the seam DocView already marked; the doc pane and the bar share the column via flex. It moves to the true end of the document with #5 without changes here.
- #24: section chips are buttons that toggle that reaction (aria-pressed = mine); the picker stays open after a pick (several reactions in one go; AC-24.14's "Enter adds a chip, then Esc closes"), and closes on Esc (focus back on the trigger), an outside click or focus leaving it.
- #24: reactions refresh on useSync's poll through a new `onPoll` option (called on every poll, also when the doc answered 304 — reactions do not change the doc ETag); no timer of its own. Clicks send the wanted state (`on: true|false`), one request per reaction at a time, so rapid clicks converge on the server state.
- #24: the button and chip borders use `--text-secondary` (≥ 3:1 against the surface in all six themes; `--text-muted` is 2.9:1 in default dark).
- #24: `GET /library/docs` items now carry `reaction_count` (00 §8: "null until #24"); `server/test-items/20-sqlite-storage.test.mjs` asserted the pre-#24 `null` and now expects `0` for a doc without reactions.
- #24 (fix round): reactions are hidden on pinned revisions (`/d/<x>@<hash>`) and file routes — they belong to the live doc, and a pinned revision is a read-only snapshot. "Who reacted" shows the name stored with each reaction: after a reader renames themselves, their entry keeps the old name until they react again (the "You" entry is still theirs).
- #24 (fix round): a reactions GET that started before a click or before a POST answer is dropped (a write counter), so a slow poll never flips a just-clicked button back. Headings whose id the server would reject (today's slugger has no length cap) get no trigger. In the content column only the doc panes (preview, editor, file view) share out the height; every other child keeps its natural height (#28's notice will sit in the same column).
- #24 (fix round): a non-string `name` in a reaction POST is treated as no name (anonymous), not a 400 — the name is optional decoration. Tabbing out of the picker (past its last or first option) closes it and returns focus to the trigger; focus moving elsewhere closes it too, except when the whole window loses focus. Keyboard focus on a doc button or chip shows "who reacted" like hover; mouse events synthesised by a touch are ignored so a long-press tooltip closes after 2 s.
- #24 (landed on #3 + #5): `sectionReactions` is registered in #3's `src/preview/enhancers.ts` right after `headingAnchors` (no separate `src/preview/index.ts`; it ignores the context today), so section keys are #3's GitHub-slugger ids; in #5's document-scroll read view the preview takes its natural height, so the reaction bar sits at the true end of the document (00 §4.2 stack), not beside it in the comments aside. Print hides the reaction bar with the other chrome (section chips are already covered by `.preview-pane button`).
- #25: a reader's row keeps `is_editor = 1` for the day once a view carried a valid edit token (max of the day's posts), so an author who also opens the doc without the token that day is still not counted. On a legacy (link-editable) doc a token proves nothing and every view counts.
- #25: a later view the same day with an empty name never erases the name already on the row; `anonymous_readers` = reader ids with no named row among the non-editor rows.
- #25: a pinned revision (`/d/<x>@<hash>`) records a view of the doc with that revision; on the doc route the revision is the content hash the sync holds, so an editor's autosaves (new revisions) re-post the view — harmless, it is the same row of the day.
- #25: `GET /paste/:id/views` is `Cache-Control: no-store` with `Vary: Authorization, X-Edit-Token` (the body depends on the token). `GET /library/docs` items carry `view_count` (= total_views) and `sort=views` orders by it (00 §8 "falls back while unavailable" no longer applies); `server/test-items/20-sqlite-storage.test.mjs` asserted the pre-#25 `null` and now expects `0` for an unviewed doc.
- #25: view-stats is a button only when the stats came with `readers` (the server decides who is an editor); the readers panel is a non-modal dialog (Esc closes and refocuses view-stats, an outside click closes) anchored under the button, a bottom sheet on a phone.
- #25 (fix round): a reader who sets a name after their view was counted posts the view once more (the same row of the day gains the name); later renames are not new views. The view stats reload when this browser's edit access changes (a rotated token turns the reader list off). The readers panel closes on an Esc nothing inside handled (bubble phase), so an overlay opened above it closes first.
- #25 (fix round): a non-string `name` in a view POST counts as no name (like #24). MCP `get_views` adds a `warning` when an edit token was sent but did not unlock the reader list (the REST read never fails on a token). The readers panel is placed inside the viewport (right-aligned with view-stats when there is room) — at tablet widths view-stats sits at the left of doc-meta-row.
- #7: the line ↔ offset map is a piecewise-linear list of anchors built from every preview block's (start, top) and (end, bottom), offsets kept monotonic — the same as interpolating inside the deepest block containing the line, and it also maps blank lines between blocks; one map serves both directions so they invert each other.
- #7: the sync toggle sits in a 36px "Preview" bar at the top of the preview pane (same height as the editor toolbar, so the panes line up); below 960px it shows on the Preview tab, and with sync on switching tabs opens the newly shown pane where the reader was in the other.
- #7: in split view the preview drops its 50em max-width but keeps the centred column through padding, so its scrollbar sits at the pane edge instead of floating mid-pane.
- #7: the HTML bridge's `scroll-ratio` reports surface as a `scroll` event on the iframe element, so SplitView listens for every pane's scrolls in one capturing listener; echoes of parent-set positions are dropped inside the frame.
- #7: the dev `?filePath=` loader now honours `?view=` (edge case "`?view=split&filePath=…` still works"); before, it always opened the read view.
- #7: a pointer click on the Edit tab (narrow split) moves the caret back into the editor, so typing and Ctrl/Cmd+Z work at once (AC-07.14 read literally); arrow-key tab navigation keeps focus on the tabs (WAI-ARIA tabs pattern).
- #7: the divider sits before the editor pane in the DOM (CSS `order` draws it between the panes), so forward Tab reaches it before the editor, which keeps Tab for indenting (#9); the sync toggle follows the editor and is reached with Esc then Tab, the documented way out of the editor.
- #7: an HTML doc's iframe restores its last scroll ratio after every reload of the *same* doc (read view too, e.g. a remote update no longer jumps to the top); another doc starts at its top or its `#fragment`, and loads without the split-view debounce.
- #13: the floating `focus-controls` sit at the right end of the rightmost toolbar row — the editor toolbar in Edit, the preview bar in wide Split, and below 960px the toolbar/preview bar under the split tabs (the tabs keep their full width) — which reserves room for them (`--focus-controls-w`, published by the cluster), so they never cover a control or a tab; on phones/touch those rows grow to 44px for the 40×40 exit button, and the editor's first line gets 12px extra top padding in focus mode.
- #13: in focus mode the comments column collapses to zero width rather than unmounting: the selection action bar and comment popover (rendered by CommentsLayer, position: fixed) stay usable, and the sidebar's own state (collapsed, filters, scroll) is untouched on exit. Banners are hidden with `v-show` for the same reason, and the header sits in a `display: contents` slot hidden with `v-show` (it is a two-root component), so it stays mounted.
- #13: Esc layering — the comment action bar / popover (00 §3.4 layer 5) is closed in a window capture listener before CodeMirror sees the key; CodeMirror's search panel and selection simplify (layers 7–8) and the modals mark or swallow their Esc; focus mode exits in a bubble listener only when nothing else took the key and no dialog is open. The editor has no multi-cursor (`allowMultipleSelections` is off), so layer 8 is "collapse a non-empty selection".
- #13 (orchestrator product call): History stays reachable in focus mode — `focus-history-btn` appears in the editor toolbar while focus mode is on, for docs with a history (as `menu-history`), and opens the same RevisionsModal; Esc closes the dialog first (whether a dialog was open is recorded in the capture phase, since Vue removes it between listeners), a second Esc exits focus mode. The view toggle stays in the hidden header, so "Edit ↔ Split keeps focus mode on" holds in code (only leaving the editing views or the doc turns it off) but has no chrome path in focus mode.
- #13: Esc closing the comment action bar / popover (00 §3.4 layer 5) applies in every view, not just focus mode; a popover holding a typed comment is never closed by Esc (in focus mode that Esc is swallowed, so it does not leave focus mode either). A held Esc or Mod+Shift+Enter acts once (`e.repeat` ignored); the shortcut does nothing under an open dialog.
- #13: contract for later layers (#12 slash menu, #15 zoom viewer, #24 reaction picker and other 00 §3.4 layer-2/3 panels): handle Esc with `preventDefault()` (or be listed in DocView's `OPEN_LAYERS`), otherwise the same Esc also exits focus mode.
- #13: the 860px Edit-view column is a DocView rule on `:deep(.cm-editor)` (next to the other focus-mode layout rules), not in EditorPane; the header stays mounted while hidden, so a filename edit in progress when the shortcut is pressed is committed (entering moves focus to the editor, and the field commits on blur), not lost.
- #13: the exit button shows an ×, distinct from the toolbar's pressed focus toggle (neutral ink on `--bg-page`, not the accent).
- #7 landing: with #10/#11/#21/#24/#25 the entry chunk sat 151 bytes under #6's AC-06.8 cap (574,644 bytes, measured under vitest's NODE_ENV=test build), which split view exceeds; dialogs that render on demand (PromptModal, ShareModal, ShareRequiredDialog), the landing FileUpload screen and the library page (DashboardView) became async components — each chunk loads when first rendered, no behaviour change. Later items adding to the shell must offload code the same way.
- #13 landing: FocusControls is an async component too (it renders only in focus mode), keeping the entry chunk within #6's AC-06.8 cap.
- #14: toolbar text (label, Copy) uses `--text-secondary`, not the spec's `--text-muted`: `--text-muted` fails AC-14.9's 4.5:1 in Default light (#8a8480 on #f0ebe2 ≈ 3.3:1).
- #14: the `<pre>` stays the visible code box (#1's frozen tests pin its background/border/radius); the toolbar is absolutely positioned from the `.code-block` wrapper over the top strip of that box — outside the `<pre>`, so it never scrolls with long lines — and the `<pre>` reserves the strip as extra top padding (rule 12: never over the first line; print drops the strip). A commented `<pre>` keeps its highlight but not its negative-margin shift, so it stays under the toolbar.
- #14: a mousedown on the code toolbar is prevented and stopped at the pane (rule 9: no selection change, no comment-flow events); the mouseup is stopped only when its mousedown was on the toolbar too, so a drag-selection ending over the toolbar still raises the comment bar. Consequence: an open comment popover stays open across a copy click (its draft is kept) — intended, do not "fix".
- #14: `copyText`'s execCommand fallback returns focus to the element that had it (the fallback focuses a hidden textarea), and always removes the textarea; this also benefits copy-link and heading anchors.
- #14: app-only nodes inside the rendered markdown carry `data-export-strip` (code toolbar, the pane's `code-copy-status` live region) so #19's export can drop them with one selector.
- #16: callouts are a core rule right after `inline`: a blockquote whose first child paragraph starts on the blockquote's first line with the marker becomes the alert `<div>` (it keeps the blockquote's token, so its line range); the title is a new paragraph token with no map; the body keeps the paragraph minus its first line (map shifted by one) and is re-parsed inline, so linkify/typographer/heading ids still run on it.
- #16: the callout title is `display: block` (icon inline, 8px gap) in every theme, GitHub included — github-markdown-css's `display: flex` drops the spaces around inline markup in a custom title ("Data**loss**risk"); GitHub's own titles have no custom text, so it never shows there. Inline markup in a title takes the title colour.
- #16: callout colours are tokens in style.css (`--callout-<type>` accent, `--callout-<type>-fg` title text, `--callout-tint`); Locus uses brand hues for edges/icons (important = `--accent`, caution = the Locus status red `--cat-must-fix`, so warning and caution never read as two oranges) with deeper/lighter text shades that pass 4.5:1. RAG pills are `--rag-<colour>-bg|fg|dot` (light and dark sets; Locus swaps in brand dots). Print maps dark themes back to the light text sets (paper is white, backgrounds may drop) and gives pills a 1px border.
- #16: a RAG label longer than the column is cut with an ellipsis (`max-width: 100%`; full label in `title`), so a valid 80-char label never scrolls a phone page sideways while the pill still never wraps.
- #16: RAG labels unescape backslash escapes only (`\]`); HTML entities stay as typed (`AT&amp;T` shows `AT&amp;T`), it is plain text. No word-boundary rule: `foo:rag-red[x]` is a badge (the spec does not forbid it; #12 always inserts with a leading space).
- #16: MCP `create_session` descriptions (both servers) name the alert and RAG syntax so agents emit it.
- #17: fold state lives in `useFolding.ts` (pure section/level/key logic + localStorage) and the `folding` enhancer (DOM); the TOC reaches the preview through `foldUi` (a `foldable` flag + the active pane's controller), so TocPanel needs no prop/injection change. Raw-HTML headings (no id) end sections but get no toggle (their state could not be keyed).
- #17: the fold key is re-computed when the doc's id settles after the render (a restored draft shows before the GET names the id; identical text does not re-render); sharing a local doc carries its folds over from `local:<filename>` to the new id.
- #17: auto-expand hooks — a synchronous router watcher (fragment changes, Back/Forward: the target is visible before PreviewPane scrolls), a document capture-phase click on `#` links in the pane or TOC (a same-fragment TOC click changes no route), `beforematch`, and a `preview-reveal` event PreviewPane's `scrollToLine` dispatches on its target (one line). The load-time reveal runs once per doc visit (cleared on route change) and only once the target exists, so Edit → Read, re-mounts and live updates never undo a fold the reader made under the same URL fragment.
- #17: no `aria-controls` on fold toggles: the folded blocks have no ids and giving them ids would collide with heading/anchor ids; the accessible name ("Fold/Unfold section X") and `aria-expanded` carry the state.
- #17: folded blocks get `hidden="until-found"` plus, on screen, zero height/margin/padding/border (until-found keeps the box, so margins and e.g. a GitHub `<hr>` would otherwise still show); print restores them (`content-visibility: visible`, and `display: block` for Safari's plain-hidden fallback, tables excepted) and opens closed `<details>` via `::details-content`.
- #17: on touch and below 1100px (16/24px side padding is no gutter for a 24–44px button) the toggle sits inline before the heading text, always shown at reduced opacity, so top-level headings are indented by it there (headings inside quotes/lists are not foldable and are not indented). On desktop it sits in the left gutter.
- #17: fold controls carry `data-preview-control`; PreviewPane's comment flow ignores mousedown/mouseup on such targets (instead of the controls stopping propagation), so document-level outside-click handlers still close menus/popovers. The ellipsis glyph is CSS (`::before`) — controls add no text to the heading (00 §2.5).
- #15: the viewer is `ZoomViewer.vue`, lazy-imported on first open and mounted by the `zoom` enhancer as its own small Vue app on `<body>` (no App/DocView change); it gets a snapshot (cloned SVG with ids suffixed `-zv` and its own `<style>`/`url(#…)` refs rewritten, or a new `<img>`), so live re-renders never touch it and the in-page SVG is never altered. Mermaid triggers are marked by a MutationObserver as each SVG lands (diagrams render after the enhancers run).
- #15: content is sized with width/height = natural × scale and moved with `translate()` only (no `scale()` transform), so SVG text stays vector-sharp and the on-screen width equals natural × scale. `zoom-content` exposes `data-scale`.
- #15: rule 8 vs rule 10: zooming (wheel, pinch, buttons, keys) keeps the point under the cursor fixed and only enforces the 48px-visible clamp; the "centre an axis smaller than the stage" part of rule 10 applies to pans and resize. Otherwise a still-small diagram would jump to the centre on every wheel tick.
- #15: keys are handled by a document capture listener while the viewer is open (focus anywhere — after a stage press, a button disabling at min/max — still reaches it), which stops propagation of every key so nothing behind it reacts (00 §3.5 "swallows everything else"); the dialog root is focusable (`tabindex=-1`) and a stage press keeps focus inside. A trigger opens on a plain Enter/Space only (no repeat, no modifier chord: Mod+Shift+Enter stays focus mode).
- #15: pointer capture retargets the click to the stage, so "background click closes" is decided by where the press landed (stage, not content) and that it was not a drag; on touch a background tap waits out the double-tap window before closing. Mouse double-click and touch double-tap share one toggle.
- #15: "Copy source" copies `dataset.source` without its final newline (as #14 copies code) and announces through a polite live region inside the dialog (the page's region is hidden by `aria-modal`); `zoom-level` is `aria-live="off"` (a wheel would announce every tick). Focus returns to the opening trigger, or the same-index trigger when the doc re-rendered meanwhile.
- #14–#17 landing (entry budget, #6 AC-06.8): every preview enhancer (#3 heading anchors, #24 section reactions, #14 code copy, #17 folding, #15 zoom) now loads from one lazy chunk (`src/preview/lazyEnhancers.ts`), requested when `enhancers.ts` loads and run as soon as it arrives if a render beats it; the folding enhancer re-aligns to the URL fragment when stored folds change the layout after that first align. Callout octicons and the code Copy/check icon are CSS masks (path data in preview.css, not in the entry JS); `foldUi` is its own tiny module so TocPanel does not pull the fold logic into the entry. Entry chunk 572,877 bytes (cap 574,644).
- #12: rule 3 vs rule 9: the menu filters by the text between `/` and the caret, but remembers how far the query was typed; the caret may move within `[/+1, end of typed query]` (←/→) without closing, and a commit replaces `/` … caret — typed text right of the caret stays and is "text after the query" (rule 13).
- #12: block items (rule 14): text after the query follows the caret when the template ends with the caret (callouts, divider, toc — like line-prefix items); otherwise (table, code, mermaid) it becomes the next paragraph after a blank line. A blank line is added after a block only when its last line is non-blank and the next doc line is non-blank (a template ending in an empty caret line already separates).
- #12: rule 13 "text precedes" does not count bare container markers: after only list/quote markers (`- `, `1. `, `> `, `- [ ] `) a line-prefix or block item takes the `/`'s place as that item's content (`- /table` → a table inside the list item, later lines indented to the content column / prefixed `> `), so no empty bullet is left behind (QA/review finding). Leading whitespace of text after the query is dropped on its new line.
- #12: an item commits on click; the menu's mousedown is prevented so the editor (or the language input) keeps focus — committing on mousedown would let the release land on the editor text below.
- #12: language step options are useMarkdown's registered hljs names plus its own extra aliases (`FENCE_LANGUAGES`); highlight.js's built-in aliases (`py`, `js`, `ts`) match too but find the canonical name, an exact name/alias match listed first, so `py` → `python` (AC-12.9) and `js` → `javascript` (not `json`). "Plain text" is filtered like the others (shown while the query is a prefix of "plain text"). Enter with no match and an invalid typed name does nothing (input `aria-invalid`, hint row); Tab = Enter; focus leaving the menu cancels like Esc.
- #12: a11y — the editor keeps role=textbox and gets `aria-controls`/`aria-haspopup=listbox`/`aria-autocomplete=list`/`aria-activedescendant` while open (CodeMirror autocomplete's pattern). The scrolling listbox is `tabindex=0` (axe scrollable-region-focusable only exempts popups of a role=combobox, which a multi-line editor is not) and hands any focus it receives straight back to the editor, whose ↑/↓ drive it; Tab in the editor commits while open, so the menu is never a tab stop in practice.
- #12: the menu is a fixed layer on `document.body` (or the fullscreen element), z-index 200, placed under the `/` and flipped above when it does not fit; it lives in the lazy editor chunk with its CSS (`src/editor/slashMenu.css`).
- #12: front matter in the editor = line 1 is `---` and a later `---`/`...` line (first 1000 lines) closes it; an unclosed leading `---` is a thematic break and the menu opens.
- #12 (tests): Playwright's `Shift+z` sends key "z", which CodeMirror resolves as Mod+Z (undo) whenever undo can run, so #12's redo checks press `Shift+Z`. #8's frozen AC-08.1 uses `Shift+z` and passes only because nothing is left to undo at that point; real keyboards send "Z" and redo works.
- #18: preview.css type sizes are `calc(N * var(--rpx))` (`--rpx` = 1px × `--reader-scale`), not em: em is relative to the parent, so code in a table cell or a heading and the frontmatter table would change size at 100% (rule 3 wants every 100% size unchanged). The reading column is still capped in em (50em of the pane's scaled size). 00 §4.6's "converts it to em" is met in intent: every type size follows the reader's scale.
- #18: the GitHub look's base becomes 16px as the spec says (`:root .preview-pane.github-mode`); before, `:root .preview-pane { font-size: 15px }` out-ranked github-markdown-css's `.markdown-body` 16px, so GitHub read at 15px. A visible change for GitHub readers (h1 30→32px).
- #18: the prefs act through `<html>` (`--reader-scale`, `data-reader-width`), set before first paint by a second inline script in index.html (no flash at a stored size) and kept current by `useReaderPrefs`; the pane's `data-reader-font-scale` / `data-reader-width` are mirrored by a lazy preview enhancer (`src/preview/readerState.ts`). The panel (`ReaderSettings.vue`), the composable and the phone overflow item (`headerMenuExtras.ts`) are lazy chunks — the #6 entry budget had ~1.7 KB left; #18 costs ~0.6 KB of it (static `data-testid`, two async-component hooks).
- #18: print resets `--reader-scale` to 1 (print.css): the on-screen text size is a screen preference; print sizing stays #5's. The #19 HTML export likewise renders at 100%.
- #18: the panel stays open when the light/dark toggle is clicked (spec edge case "panel restyles, values intact"); every other outside click closes it. On a phone, Esc / close returns focus to `header-overflow-btn` (the control's home there).
- #18: AC-18.9 "the iframe bounding box equals the main pane's" — #24's reaction bar sits under the iframe in the main pane, so the e2e test checks that the iframe spans the main pane's width and that its box is identical with and without stored prefs (the intent: prefs never touch HTML docs).
- #18 (frozen-test change): `tests/e2e/items/17-collapsible.test.mjs` AC-17.2's text walker rejected text under any `[data-testid]` ancestor; #18 rule 6 puts `data-testid="preview-pane"` on the pane itself, so every heading text was rejected. Minimal fix: exclude `[data-testid="preview-pane"]` from that ancestor test.
- #19: the desktop Download trigger is icon-only (download glyph, `aria-label`/title "Download") so the bar still fits at 1100px; tablet/phone get the "Download" group in the overflow menu (00 §2.2). It sits before `theme-toggle`, so it never carries `.btn-icon`.
- #19: the self-contained export copies the on-screen preview (read view, or split view's visible preview) into an inert document, so its images do not load; with no visible preview (edit view, or the editor tab of narrow split) it renders the editor's markdown off screen and draws the diagrams itself with the theme's mermaid config (`src/preview/mermaidTheme.ts`, extracted from PreviewPane and shared). It renders at 100% (the #18 reader scale is a screen preference), folds expanded, `<details>` as the reader left them.
- #19: the export drops every `<script>` and inline `on*` handler (and `javascript:` URLs), author HTML included — the file is a static snapshot; nothing in it needs to run. Code blocks are unwrapped to their `<pre>`, and the inlined CSS has app-chrome rules removed (copy/toolbar/fold/anchor/reaction/zoom/comment-highlight selectors), so the file carries no chrome class names at all.
- #19: the export page's background is the theme's reading surface (`--bg-surface`), i.e. what the reader sees behind the doc (github-dark #0d1117, AC-19.6); AC-19.7 compares it with the on-screen `.preview-pane` background.
- #19: PDF from the edit view (nothing printable on screen) switches to the read view for the print, waits for its diagrams (drawn for the current theme), prints, then returns to the edit view. A pinned revision's downloads are named after the doc (`docMeta.filename`; its `filename` ref holds the id).
- #19: busy state (rule 11) is the HTML export's: `aria-busy` on `download-menu-btn`, and `download-html` shows "HTML (.html) — preparing…" with `aria-busy`/`aria-disabled` wherever it is listed; while any download runs, another request is ignored (one file per click).
- #19: entry budget — `DownloadMenu.vue`, `downloadActions.ts`, `useDownload.ts` and the overflow entries (`headerMenuExtras.ts`) are lazy; the inlined CSS strings are separate chunks loaded only when an HTML export runs.
- #19: on a phone, the header's 40px minimum for its buttons also applied to the overflow sheet's items; sheet items keep their 44px rows (AC-19.14; DocHeader scoped CSS).
- #19: mermaid's config is global, so every render job (each preview, the export's off-screen render) now runs through one queue (`mermaidJob` in `src/preview/mermaidTheme.ts`); the export waits for diagrams drawn for the current theme (`data-rendered-key`), so a theme switched just before export never ships the previous theme's drawings. AppMenu gained a `triggerAttrs` prop (the Download trigger's `aria-busy`; reusable by #26/#27 menus).
- #19 (QA follow-ups): download names drop trailing dots (`dot.` → `dot.md`, never `dot..md`); exported task-list checkboxes are `disabled` (a record, not a control); on tablet the overflow menu's items get 44px rows too (AC-19.14 asks it of phones only). The export stays at 100% / 50em whatever the #18 reader settings (a screen preference, like print) — product call recorded above.
- #6 (entry budget): highlight.js keeps 11 common languages in the entry (javascript, typescript, json, bash, shell, python, yaml, xml/html, markdown, diff, plaintext); the other 25 load as one small chunk each on first use (`src/markdown/highlight.ts`). Shared/pinned docs wait up to 300 ms for their fences' lazy languages before the first render, so code paints with colours; past that (slow network) or for a language first typed in the editor, the fence shows as plain text until its chunk arrives, then the preview re-renders (`highlightRevision`). HTML export waits for them. Saves ~91 KB of entry JS.
- #28: `GET /paste/:id` adds `view` + `agentSections` only when the request carries `?view=` (the default full response keeps its legacy shape); `GET /paste/:id/markdown` always adds them (rule 17). `/comments` ignores `view`. An invalid `view` on `/paste/*` → 400 JSON `{error}`; on `/d/:x.md` → 400 text/plain — matches each route's existing error format.
- #28: `/d/:x.md` ETag is content-addressed (`"raw-<md5(source)>"`, human variant `…-h"`), `/paste/:id[/markdown]` keeps `sessionEtag` with `-h` appended for human — rule 18 with the smallest change to existing ETags (agent/default ETags are unchanged).
- #28: MCP `rawUrl` base = `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` when set, else `PASTE_PUBLIC_URL`/`PASTE_API_URL` (the backend origin clients already use). A plain `get_session` (no `view`, no `fields`) keeps its legacy URL and derives `agentSections` with the same shared strip, so older clients/tests see no request change.
- #28: `/llms.txt` uses absolute URLs only when `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is set explicitly (else server-relative paths, never a localhost default); `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.
- #28: the `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` is emitted only on the live markdown doc's meta page — not for HTML docs, pinned revisions, session files or 404/410 pages (raw endpoints for those are out of scope).
- #28: the server's display derivations (`docTitle`, #22 description) now run on `shared/agentSections.mjs`'s human view; #22's own approximate agent-skipping inside `firstH1`/`markdownBlocks` was removed (it disagreed with the shared rules for markers in lists/quotes). A cheap `/<!--\s*agent/i` precheck skips the strip for ordinary docs (keeps the AC-22 1 MB perf budget).
- #28: from the edit view (no preview on screen) the .html export and PDF render the read view, i.e. the human view (#19 rule 8 and its frozen test); the edit view's `.md` download is the full source (rule 13). Split view exports its preview, which shows agent sections. — keeps #19's "print what the read view shows" contract.
- #28: agent view is a reading view: the view toggle shows Read pressed in it, and clicking Read returns to the human view (`view=read`); `agent-view-exit` removes `view`.
- #28: the TOC follows the view (agent view lists headings inside agent sections); `docTitle` always uses the human view (00 §5).
- #28: the notice and the banner are lazy components (off the #6 entry chunk); the strip/range finder and the markdown plugin are eager (the first render needs them, and loading them later would flash hidden content).
- #28: `tests/composables/useRouter.test.ts` "allowed but not shipped" no longer uses `agent` (it ships with #28); a new case pins agent resolution (doc/pinned allowed, embed read, `AGENT` rewritten). Pre-existing test change, not a frozen item test.
- #28: the shared line scanner tracks every CommonMark HTML block type (1–7; type 7 only when it cannot be a paragraph continuation), so a marker line inside an HTML block is literal for the server and the FE alike; a differential unit test asserts the human render shows exactly the stripped text for every fixture.
- #28: no raw link (`agent-raw-link`, head alternate link) on pinned revisions — the raw endpoint serves the latest version.
- #29: printing slides, every slide but the last has `break-after: page`; the last is `auto`, because Chromium prints a blank extra page after a forced break at the end of the document (AC-29.16's "each with break-after: page" read as "one slide per page").
- #29: slides print with #5's light print palette (like the read view), except the title slide, which keeps `--slide-title-bg/fg` (so the Locus title slide prints purple with white text); backgrounds are printed (`print-color-adjust: exact`).
- #29: an in-doc `#heading` link on a slide goes to the slide holding that heading (instead of changing the URL fragment); other links behave as links and never count as a half-canvas click.
- #29: the canvas renders every slide (only the current one is visible, in the accessibility tree and in the tab order — `inert` + `aria-hidden` on the others), so diagrams lay out off screen, fit is measured once per render and print emits all slides.
- #29: on-canvas type scales with the preview's own unit (`--rpx` = 1.6px × the fit factor); fit steps down by 5% to 70%, then the slide scrolls.
- #29: a heading inside a `<!-- notes -->` block is on no slide (notes are off the canvas), so `#that-id` opens slide 1.
- #29: diagrams on a slide are sized to fit (≤ the body width, ≤ the room under the content before them, never upscaled past mermaid's own width); the read view's diagram sizing is unchanged.
- #29: below 500px of viewport height (landscape phones) the slide controls float over the canvas and auto-hide after 3 s idle like in fullscreen, so the canvas fills the height (rule 17).
