- #29: #5's print sheet still styles slides (light palette, chrome hidden); the deck's print block undoes what clips a fixed-size slide (#5's printed link URLs) and hides mermaid's body-level tooltip (which added a blank page).
- #29: the zoom viewer (#15) mounts inside the fullscreen element when there is one (in fullscreen only its subtree is drawn).
- #29: on a portrait phone the 1280-wide canvas makes body text small (~5px); that is the spec's scaled-canvas model, and the rotate hint is the remedy.
- fix-api (persona agent #6): a comment/reply on a publish-mode doc is accepted (stored, shown once the doc is switched to review) and flagged: REST sends `X-MdReview-Warning` + `X-MdReview-Visible: false` headers, MCP adds `visible:false` + `warning` to the result — keeps agents working; headers rather than body keys keep #20's legacy JSON shapes.
- fix-api (persona agent #7 / engineer m4): approval follows the content — any content change to an approved doc resets it to pending (`approval_reset_at` set, the approval webhook gets `{approval_status:"pending", reason:"content_changed"}`); approvals record `approved_revision` (GET /approval shows it). changes_requested is not reset (the author is expected to change the doc).
- fix-api (persona agent #5): renaming a slug keeps the old slug as an alias of the same doc (links already handed out keep working; the meta page's canonical/redirect goes to the new slug). Removing the slug (`""`) releases it. Deleting the doc frees every alias. One golden entry (#20 'meta A: old slug gone') is allowed to differ for this.
- fix-api (persona agent #16): comment anchors are checked only for non-UI clients (the editor may hold unsaved lines): lines past the end of the doc are a 400 `invalid_anchor` (one line of slack keeps 1-based inclusive ranges valid); a selectedText not found in the source is accepted with a warning. Reactions on unknown section ids stay accepted (#24: the server never parses headings).
- fix-api (persona agent #14): create results converge on {id, slug, mode, url, viewUrl, app_url, editToken, editUrl} in MCP and CLI; REST POST /paste keeps its legacy shape (no `slug` key when there is none, #20 goldens) and the mixed `app_url`/camelCase names and epoch-ms comment timestamps stay for compatibility. MCP get_reactions keeps #24's emoji-keyed shape (frozen) and adds a `codes` emoji→code map.
- fix-api (persona agent #22): the cover keeps "Markdown" in both the pill and the meta line (#22 rule 8 / AC-22.11 mandate both); the weekly-cover cue is the "Updated D Mon YYYY" date already in the meta line.
- fix-api (persona agent #23): a pinned revision's meta page says "(earlier revision)" in `<title>`/`<h1>` only (og:title stays the revision's title, AC frozen in 22-fixes); `/d/x@rev.md` serves that revision raw. Session files have no raw `/d/` route: `/paste/x/files/<name>` is the raw route (documented in /llms.txt).
- fix-api (persona agent #12): MCP `sessionId` also accepts an upsert key (it contains ':', '.' or '_', which ids and slugs never do) and resolves it via GET /paste/by-key; anything that is not an id, slug or key is refused before it reaches an API path or shell command.
- #9 (QA M5): new rule 1f — with an empty selection, Mod+B/I/Shift+X/E inside an empty pair (`**|**`) removes the pair, and right before the closer of a span opened earlier on the line (`**bb|**`, closer not preceded by whitespace) steps over it. Like Docs' bold-off; rule 1d still applies everywhere else.
- #8/#21 (QA M6): PUT /paste/:id/markdown takes `overwrite: true` (sent only by "Keep my version"); that write never coalesces, so the overwritten copy stays its own revision. "Use server version" sets the local edits aside as the #23 local copy (`reason: 'conflict'`, with a Restore button) and History lists it as a "Your set-aside edits" row. History rows are keyed by position, not hash (a restore repeats an older hash; only the newest is "now"); re-clicking the FROM row no longer deselects it.
- #2/#21 (QA leader M4): for a viewer, History opens on a summary — the change notes in the compared range and the sections the diff touches — with the raw line diff behind "Show line-by-line changes". Editors still get the diff at once (plus the summary).
- #10 (QA m7): an image inserted on the line right after a GFM table (or at the end of its last row) gets a leading break so it starts its own paragraph instead of becoming a table row.
- persona-QA read lane: a leading front-matter block renders as its Field/Value table only for editors and in review mode (comment anchors need its lines); a view-link reader of a publish-mode doc (read/agent/embed, and so its print/HTML export) sees the doc without it. The front-matter `title:` still drives docTitle. Editors keep the table so AC-05.2 / AC-05.19 behaviour and authoring visibility are unchanged.
- persona-QA read lane: "Open file…" is offered only when no doc is open or to editors; a view-link reader of a shared doc never sees it.
- persona-QA read lane: on a landscape phone (< 500px tall) whose letterbox beside the full-height canvas is ≥ 56px, the slide controls sit in the side rails (exit / prev / notes left, fullscreen / next / counter right) and do not auto-hide; with no such room they float and auto-hide as before. The canvas still fills the height (rule 17).
- persona-QA read lane: the zoom viewer keeps #15's initial scale (fit, AC-15.4) and "Copy source" for every reader (engineers reading a shared link reuse diagram source); the phone fix is the tap itself (a touch click lands several px from the touch point, so the drag check now measures pointerdown → pointerup).
- persona-QA read lane: mermaid labels never inherit the doc's text rules (Locus p/li size, colour, line height, #18 scale, slides' larger type), because mermaid measures label boxes off-screen; after each render a label below 3:1 on an author `style … fill:` switches to dark or white text (labels with an author `color:` are left alone).
- persona-QA read lane: a crowded desktop reader bar (review mode) first moves the meta items (updated / badges / views) to doc-meta-row, then shows Home, Library and Copy link as icons; the doc title always keeps ≥ 160px (or its full width).
- persona-QA read lane: on touch the heading-anchor sits at the right end of the heading's first line, out of the text flow (it wrapped onto a line of its own), and the fold toggle sits in a 32px indent of the heading (no hanging first line). DOM order (00 §2.5) is unchanged.
- persona-QA read lane: a blank local doc (untitled.md) is renamed after its title (`capacity-plan.md`) until the user renames it; shared docs keep their server filename.
- persona-QA read lane: "Start blank" still opens the read view (app.test relies on it) but an empty doc there shows "This document is empty. Start writing", which opens the editor. The paste flow's button reads "Open document" (app.test updated).
- persona-QA read lane: the approval banner asks for a name only while the header has none; the name used to approve becomes the header name. The comments badge counts open comments (a check when all are resolved). Review statuses use new `--status-*` tokens (Locus: brand green/amber); existing token names are unchanged. The Review Summary's collapsed state is remembered per browser.
- persona-QA read lane: print keeps #5's "cells wrap anywhere" for tables (a name can still split mid-word on paper) — break-word would let a 12-column table overflow A4 (AC-05.11's last-column check).
- #26 (server): a `name:` reader key is compared trimmed and lower-cased server-side (`name:Asha` ≡ `name:asha`); an empty `X-MdReview-Reader` counts as absent. The pin limit (50) counts only pins of existing, unexpired docs, so an expired pinned doc frees its slot; re-pinning an already pinned doc at the limit is a no-op 200. Pinning an expired doc → 410 (like reactions); PUT tags/collection on an expired doc → 410 after the edit check.
- #26 (server): `POST /library/pins/merge` only adds: the source's pins (most recently pinned first, original `pinnedAt` kept) are copied until the target holds 50; the target's own pins are never dropped.
- #26 (server): tags and collection names sort in code-point order of the (lower-cased) text — the same comparator (`compareTags`, shared/tags.mjs) for `tags` arrays in /library/docs, `?fields=library`, `PUT …/tags` and `GET /library/tags`. Tag lower-casing is ASCII-only, so a non-ASCII letter that lower-cases to ASCII (KELVIN SIGN) stays invalid.
- #26 (server): a collection's `slug` is regenerated on rename (unique among collections; never `none` or another collection's id); filters and links use the id. Tag/collection changes, collection renames and deletes bump the affected docs' `version`, so `GET /paste/:id?fields=library` never answers a stale 304.
- #26 (server): document-file index rows are found by scanning doc_fts (session_id/file_name are UNINDEXED and schema_version stays 1), so the scan runs only for document files — never for pasted images or other attachments — and on session delete only when the session has document files (~5 ms per doc-file write at 400 × 48 KB docs). A boot-time backfill indexes document files that have no row (migrated data); the migration script itself is unchanged.
- #26 (server): `GET /library/docs?pinned=1` (for the library's pinned section): only the header reader's pins, `pinned_at DESC` unless a sort is given; no header → `items: []`; `pinned=0`/absent = no filter, any other value → 400; `pinned` and the reader key are bound into the cursor. This is an extension beyond 00 §8 and the captain's #26 contract (which listed no `pinned` param): this line amends that contract, so MCP and #27+ may rely on it (tests: server/test-items/26-library.test.mjs).
- #26: the library's row heights are known without measuring (`libraryRowHeight`): desktop rows are fixed (68 px, 90 px with a search snippet); a phone card is 2 lines (76 px + an 8 px gap), + 28 px for its tags line only when that line has content (tags, a collection, or "+ tag" for editors), + 24 px for a snippet (fix round, QA c1: no empty band). The phone list positions its window from per-row offsets (prefix sums; `virtualRange` binary-searches them). Row text never wraps (ellipsis), and the window is capped at 120 − (pinned rows shown) so pinned + main rows stay ≤ 120 in the DOM.
- #26: "Clear filters" resets q and every filter but keeps an explicitly chosen sort (sort is not a filter, rule 6); with no chosen sort the URL is the bare /library. Choosing the sort that is the default for the current q (Recently updated without q, Relevance with q) removes `sort` from the URL (fix round, QA m2), so a later search defaults to relevance again. A URL `q` of one character stays in the box but sends no search (list mode, sections shown).
- #26: the library header carries the reviewer-name control (ReviewerName) and the theme switcher, so pins can follow a name from the library itself; the App-level app bar now shows only on the not-found page. The pin merge (POST /library/pins/merge) runs from App.vue whenever the name goes from empty to set, on any page.
- #26: a row click anywhere outside its controls opens the doc (pushState); the title is a real link (`/d/<slug or id>`) so open-in-new-tab works. Bulk "not_found" results count as done (the doc is gone either way); only edit_token_required/invalid count as "skipped — no edit access".
- #26: the recent list is recorded when a shared doc at /d/:slug is on screen (not embeds, pinned revisions or file routes), and re-recorded when its title changes while open; recent items render as links even for docs deleted elsewhere (they open the doc view's not-found state, per the spec's edge case). Fix round (QA m3): a 404/410 on `/d/:x` falls back to this browser's local copy only when its persisted draft of that doc has unsaved edits; a clean draft (the doc was only viewed) gives `doc-not-found` like any unknown doc. The offline (server unreachable) fallback is unchanged. Title changes of the open doc are recorded debounced (800 ms), and the recording code is a lazy chunk (`noteRecent` in useRecent.ts).
- #26: a file route keeps its doc attached (same GET, capability, poll and unsaved-edit guard); the doc's markdown stays in the doc state and the file renders from a separate store (useSessionFiles), so autosave can never write a file's text into the doc. Consequence: `GET /paste/:id` is now made on a direct file-route load (04-routes-extra "no live-doc GET" assertion dropped), and switching doc ↔ file tab never reloads or re-prompts.
- #26: on file routes `capability` is the doc's (00 §1.2) but `view` is always read and `reviewUI` is false (resolveDocAxes), so no editor, view toggle, comments, approval or prompt there; the doc's stored mode is untouched. DocHeader hides `view-toggle` on file routes (one-line change).
- #26: the file list comes from the doc's own payloads (its first GET and every changed poll carry `files`), plus `GET /paste/:id?fields=library` for the collection after each of them; after this browser adds/removes a file it re-reads `GET /paste/:id/files`. A file that disappears from the list while open turns into `file-not-found`.
- #26: every tab (primary included) is `data-testid="file-tab"` with `role="tab"`, `data-file` (= the path, '' for the primary); `file-tab-remove` is the tab's sibling button (same `data-file`), not nested in the tab (no nested interactive). Attachments are removed from a "Remove" group in the attachments menu (items also `file-tab-remove`).
- #26: viewers see the strip when the doc has any document file **or attachment** (otherwise attachments would be unreachable); editors always see it on a shared doc. Local (never-shared) docs, pinned revisions and embeds have no strip or breadcrumb.
- #26: replace/remove confirmations are in-app dialogs (fix round, QA m1): the library's confirm became the shared `ConfirmDialog.vue` (testid prefix prop: `library-confirm-*` in the library, `file-confirm-*` in the file strip), a 00 §3.4 layer-2 modal that starts focused on Cancel (FE review: Enter never confirms a destructive action by accident). The leave guard (rule 13) keeps its `window.confirm` (pre-existing, #4/#8 tests). Uploads show a "Uploading <name>…" status in the strip (no byte progress), failures toast "Couldn't add <name>: <server error>". `.txt` and known code extensions render as one fenced, highlighted code block; `.csv`/unknown types are download cards (keeps #4's csv behaviour).
- #26: on phones the breadcrumb collapses the collection to a `…` link (full name in `title`), the doc title ellipsizes first and the file segment keeps up to 60% of the line.
- #26: search snippets of markdown docs and markdown files keep inline HTML tags as literal text (`markdownToPlain(md, {keepTags:true})`, used only by the snippet path; HTML comments are still removed), so AC-26.3 shows `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>kumquat` verbatim and the FE renders it as text. docTitle, the indexed content and HTML docs/files (tag-stripped, 00 §8 / AC-20.14) are unchanged.
- #26: the multi-file UI is out of the entry chunk (#6 AC-06.8 had 558 bytes of headroom at HEAD): FileTabs/DocBreadcrumb/FileView are async components and the store + helpers live in the lazy `sessionFiles.ts`; the entry keeps a ~1 KB shim (`useSessionFiles.ts`) that records the attached doc's latest payload from boot and queues file opens until the chunk loads. Entry under the test's build: 574,039 bytes (HEAD 574,086, limit 574,644).
- #26 (server): a `name:` reader key's 80-character limit is checked before lower-casing (a letter such as `İ` grows when lower-cased); tags no other doc uses are dropped when a doc is deleted (single, bulk and the expiry sweep all go through `deleteSession`); `PUT /library/pins/:docId` inserts with a plain INSERT (an existing pin row always answers first).
- #26 (server), known follow-up: finding a document file's doc_fts row scans doc_fts (its columns are UNINDEXED), which grows with total indexed bytes. When the schema version next bumps for another reason, store `fts_rowid` on the `files` row as the `sessions` row does. #26 must not bump the schema version (AC-20.1) just for this.
- #26: on a file route History, Document mode and the "changed since you last looked" banner are not offered (they act on the doc, which is out of sight there — restoring a revision or switching the mode from a file tab would change it invisibly); they are one click away on the primary tab. Copy link in the header still copies the doc's URL; a heading's copy-link inside a file copies `/d/<doc>/<file>#<id>`.
- #26: attachments download from blob URLs (the download card links one; the attachments menu fetches the file first), because `<a download>` is ignored on the cross-origin API URL (00 §9) and would navigate the app tab away. A failed fetch toasts.
- #26: the doc view re-reads `GET /paste/:id?fields=library` (the collection) on the doc's first payload and then only on payloads whose `content_hash` did not change (a collection move bumps the version alone), so a remote editor typing does not double the poll traffic. The session-files store chunk import is retried on the next payload or file open after a failure (a file open that cannot load it shows a notice).
- #26: the file strip's tabs keep `role="tab"`/`aria-selected` (the spec's hooks) and gain `aria-controls="doc-tabpanel"`; the doc body (`#doc-tabpanel`, rail + content + aside) is the `role="tabpanel"` while the strip is shown, labelled with the file (or primary doc) name.
- #26 → #27+: the #6 AC-06.8 entry-chunk budget is nearly spent (after the #26 fix round: 573,575 of 574,644 bytes under the test's build, ~1 KB left). Any later item that adds code reachable from the entry (App.vue, DocView/DocHeader/DocBanners, PreviewPane, docState/useDocLoader and their static imports) must put it behind an async boundary (defineAsyncComponent / dynamic import) and re-measure.
- #27: placeholders allow spaces/tabs inside the braces but never a line break (`{{\ntitle}}` stays verbatim), so a placeholder split across lines is never substituted. `{{{title}}}` substitutes only the inner placeholder (→ `{Value}`). Rule 8's `variables` lists every syntactically valid name, unknown ones included (a mermaid `A{{Decide}}` shows up as a `Decide` chip).
- #27: the AC-27.2 clock reuses the #25 test clock `MDREVIEW_NOW` (00 §10.5) for `{{date}}`/`{{week}}` only; the date logic is also unit-tested with an injected clock (`server/template-vars.cjs` takes `now`). No new env var.
- #27: an empty or whitespace-only `author` (or `collection`) counts as no value, so `{{author}}` stays verbatim; a custom variable with an empty string value does substitute (it was supplied explicitly).
- #27: `contentType` on `POST /templates` defaults to `markdown` when absent and `mode` to `publish`; `title` is optional for `/render` (an empty title leaves `{{title}}` verbatim so the preview works while typing) but required (1–200, trimmed) for `/instantiate`.
- #27: an unknown/deleted `collectionId` passed explicitly to `render`/`instantiate`/`POST`/`PATCH /templates` → 400 `{error, code:'unknown_collection', available}` and nothing is created; a template's *default* collection that was deleted reads as null (unfiled) instead. `collectionId: null` on instantiate overrides the template default (unfiled).
- #27: `POST /templates/:id/instantiate` (and render) also accept `collection` = id, slug or name (case-insensitive), resolved on the server; MCP `create_from_template` uses it, so it does not depend on #26's `/library/collections` endpoint. Template ids/names for MCP are resolved from `GET /templates`.
- #27: name clashes answer 409 `{error, code:'name_taken', builtin, id, name}` — `builtin:true` tells the save dialog not to offer Replace, `name` is the existing template's name (the dialog quotes it, QA D2); replace keeps the existing template's id, `created_by` and name (fix round: the clash is case/space-insensitive, so "Replace" means that template's content and fields, not a rename; renaming is PATCH).
- #27: the boot upsert also deletes builtin rows whose id left the manifest (still builtin rows only); user template ids are `tpl-<12 hex>`, so they can never collide with `seed-*`.
- #27: instantiate returns 201 `{id, slug, mode, url, viewUrl, app_url, editToken, editUrl, collection}` with `Cache-Control: no-store` (POST /paste's link fields plus the collection); `from_template` is stored only in `sessions.from_template_json`; `session-rows.cjs` decodes it into meta and `from_template` is COLUMN_OWNED, so a meta PUT can neither drop nor forge it (review fix, superseding the earlier double write).
- #27: instantiate re-reads the target collection inside its transaction; one deleted between validation and the write files the doc as unfiled (201, `collection: null`) rather than failing the FK insert with a 500.
- #27: builtin templates list in manifest order (Weekly leadership update first), from the manifest position recorded at boot; a seed whose name a user template already holds is still upserted, with a boot warning naming both.
- #27: the template dialogs never touch the entry chunk: the landing button and the overflow item call `templateEntry.ts` (one dynamic import), and `templateHost.ts` mounts TemplatePicker / SaveTemplateDialog as their own small Vue apps under <body> (router, toasts, edit tokens and reader name are module singletons, so nothing is lost). The landing page (`FileUpload.vue`) became an async component in DocView to pay for the new entry points: AC-06.8 headroom went from ~500 B to ~4.7 KB.
- #27: Save as template reads the doc state when the item is chosen (title, editor model incl. unsaved edits, contentType, mode); the dialog fetches the doc's collection for its default. Over-1 MB content is refused in the dialog before any request, with the server's own wording ("larger than 1 MB").
- #27: Esc in the picker / save dialog is a `@keydown` on the dialog element (preventDefault + stopPropagation, ignored when already defaultPrevented), like LibraryConfirmDialog, so a layer above it (#15 zoom viewer) gets Esc first (00 §3.4). Focus never leaves the dialog: while busy, Create / Save / Replace are `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`) and the dialog carries `aria-busy` and `tabindex="-1"` (fix round, replacing the earlier window capture listener). The picker closes on any navigation.
- #27: the library sections are `?tab=templates` only (Documents = no param); switching drops the documents list's query. They are a `<nav aria-label="Library sections">` of two links with `aria-current="page"` (fix round: each section is a URL, so links, not an ARIA tablist). The delete confirm reuses LibraryConfirmDialog with a new optional `testid` prop (`template-delete-confirm`). The success toast's "View templates" keeps its `href` (middle-click / new tab) and adds `onClick` → `router.push`: AppToast now runs `onClick` on a plain click of a link action instead of following the href (fix round).
- #27: the picker's preview is PreviewPane (the normal renderer) fed by the server dry run; the theme is read from the <html> classes, since the dialog is a separate Vue app without the doc state.
- #27: the template picker's preview is PreviewPane with a new `standalone` prop: links never navigate the app (an in-page `#anchor` scrolls inside the preview), no preview enhancers run (no section-link button or reactions — QA D3), no URL-fragment alignment, and the HTML frame's `anchor-changed` is ignored. The frame's sandbox is unchanged (hardening logged in POLISH.md).
- #27: closing the picker while a create is in flight never navigates: the doc is still created (its edit token kept) and a success toast "Created “X”" offers Open (`router.pushRoute(…, 'view=edit')`).
- #27: the save dialog closes when the route identity changes (`current.key`: another doc, file, pinned revision, library…) or on any Back/Forward (`source: 'pop'`); a query rewrite on the same doc (`?view=`) keeps it open.
- #27: a template's `variables` are computed on write and stored in `data_json`; `GET /templates` and name checks read rows without their content (`json_remove(data_json,'$.content')`, guarded by `json_valid`). Rows written before this (no stored list) fall back to scanning their content; seeds pick it up at the next boot upsert.
- #27: the library reaches the template dialogs through `templateEntry.ts` (`newFromTemplate()`, `newFromTemplateId(id)`), so the library chunk no longer carries them; a failed chunk load shows the error toast "Could not open templates. Reload the page." instead of doing nothing.
- #27: the lazy landing page (`src/components/lazyLanding.ts`) requests its chunk when DocView sets up on the landing route (in parallel with boot, before `booted`), and a failed load renders a "This page could not be loaded. Reload" prompt (`landing-load-error`) instead of a blank page.
- #27: in the Templates tab, focus that fell to <body> after a rename, an Esc in the rename box or a delete goes to the row's Use button (after a delete: the next row, else the previous); focus the reader put elsewhere is left alone. Blur no longer cancels a rename whose request is in flight.
- #27: "Use {{title}}" on html skips `<title>`/`<h1>` inside comments, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<template>`, `<textarea>` and `<svg>`; on markdown a fence line with an info string never closes a fence (CommonMark).
- #27: on phones the library header shows "Template" (aria-label/title "New from template") and the header buttons use 10px side padding, so "Set your name", the theme controls, Template and New fit on one line at 390px (found by the lane gate after merging #27 onto #26).
